newsitem.title: USA: Alleged Versace murderer Cunanan believed dead.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Versace murderer Cunanan believed dead.

text.p: Andrew Cunanan, the alleged killer of fashion designer Gianni Versace and four other men, appeared to have taken his own life on Wednesday after police cornered him in a houseboat on Miami Beach, authorities said.
Although officials gave no final confirmation, Miami Beach Mayor Seymour Gelber said police had told him they believed a dead man found inside the dwelling was Cunanan.

"That is the information I have received, but they have not given us final word on it," Gelber said, adding that the man had committed suicide. "The general feeling ... is that this very well may be Cunanan."

Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto told a news conference that the body of a white man who bore a "similarity" to Cunanan was found inside the houseboat after SWAT assault specialists stormed it.

Local radio station WINZ said a .40-calibre pistol also was found inside the residence, located between the site of Versace's murder and the hotel where Cunanan stayed for several weeks before the killing.

The FBI said on Tuesday that such a gun was used to kill Versace and two of the other four men Cunanan was suspected of murdering. Cunanan was on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list of fugitives even before the Versace slaying.

Barreto said forensic tests were being carried out to confirm the dead man's identity. Fans had been brought in to clear lingering tear gas fired into the houseboat earlier by police which was hampering examination of the body.
"We certainly don't want to rush the technicians, this is a very important crime scene for us, for that reason we are taking every precaution," Barreto said.
Police have a clear thumbprint of Cunanan's taken at a Miami Beach pawn shop several days before the Versace killing, when he hocked a gold coin allegedly stolen from one of his previous victims.
Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza, briefing Spanish-speaking reporters, said the body had a gunshot wound and that police did not fire any shots while storming the houseboat earlier on Wednesday.
Boza earlier said the houseboat was found empty after an initial search. The body appeared to have been discovered during a second more thorough search.

Dozens of police including heavily armed SWAT teams surrounded the houseboat after its caretaker reported a man resembling Cunanan had fired a shot when he approached the site around 4 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT).
Four hours later, police fired tear gas into the houseboat and then entered the two-level dwelling. They met no response and could later be seen leaving in a relaxed manner.
Local television said the owner of the boat was identified as a German citizen who also owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. Police described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.

Versace, who dressed the world's beautiful people in flamboyant and sexy couture, was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the trendy Art Deco South Beach area of Miami Beach.
Versace was also a homosexual but there was no confirmation the two men had a relationship.

Variously described as a gay prostitute down on his luck and a charming, intelligent chameleon who could change his appearance at will, Cunanan blurred the lines between the usual categories applied to multiple murderers, experts in the field said.

They said Cunanan began as a "spree killer" set off by a desire for vengeance against a known victim, then developed a taste for cruelty shared by serial killers, and finally sought the infamy perceived by mass murderers.
Police said they believed he could have disguised himself as a woman to try to elude police during the nine-day manhunt he sparked.
He was also wanted for the murders of his former lover Jeffrey Trail, 28, in late April; their mutual friend David Madson, 33, in May; Lee Miglin, 72, also in May; and William Reese, 45, also in May.
In an ironic twist, his death, if confirmed, coincided with a passionate plea to Cunanan to give himself up from a close friend issued Wednesday by the FBI.
"The time has come for this to end peacefully," Elizabeth Cote, who said Cunanan was godfather to her children, wrote in the letter.
